chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Refusing an encore until Harry Richman quieted the house
summary: He refuses to go back up until Buck presses him; Richman quiets the audience, the stage manager complains, and Nazarro likes it.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: However, when I come down-stairs they're hollering "Buck and Bubbles, Buck and Bubbles." They're hollering "Buck and Bubbles." And up on the stage they're asking if Buck and Bubbles are coming back and Buck is calling me, "Come on, Bubba," I said, "No, forget about it, forget it." And he doesn't know why I'm saying this. Neither does the stage manager know, neither does my manager. My manager is out in the front watching the show.
Nobody knows why I'm saying this and don't care about going back on stage but me.

So finally I decide for Buck I'll go back since he don't know. So I went back up on the stage -- soon as I got on the stage where you go on the stage, Harry Richman quiets the audience down. He says, "Shh-h-h -- you know there's a little speakeasy up the alley where Buck and Bubbles went." Somebody in the back says, "Well, go get 'em." And they start applauding again. We went on and took a bow and come on off.

Then the stage manager after that started raising Sane about leaving the stage before the audience quiets. Well he forgot -- leaving the stage I was going on and forget the whole doggone thing. But I went on downstairs again and my manager heard what he said, then the manager was in my corner because that tied up the show longer by me not going back on the stage, it tied the show up longer, made us more important, you know. And that was

right up Nazarro's alley. He wanted that. But lo and behold, when I go downstairs and get dressed and go out and I tell the manager after what had happened, I told my manager what happened, Nazarro, what had happened. He said, it fit like a glove. It's all right. I said the guy over at the lights made me mad and I just as soon not go on at all.

So from then on nobody wanted to follow us, nobody. And it changes every night. They changed the show every night. Like this night we were on next to closing, this night after us couldn't nobody get on. They put the finale on, and they figured from then on they're going to put us on and then let the finale come behind us. And that's what happened every night. So we come in, Harry Leroy and Mitzi Mayfair already did their dance -- we already did a show in Harlem, we were doubling from the Lafayette Theater to the Ziegfeld Theater. We were doubling.
